title: Latency-aware multilingual cross-encoder fusion and upgrade playbook
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: evaluate a small set of cross-encoder variants for multilingual reranking and produce a repeatable, latency-aware upgrade playbook that preserves or improves ranking quality while meeting SLOs at scale. Scope covers model candidate selection, offline/regression evaluation, latency and throughput profiling under representative workloads, canary rollout configurations, and an automated smoke + rollback policy integrated with Console rollouts.

Background: Our current rerank endpoint uses a medium-sized cross-encoder family tuned for English-heavy traffic. Increasing multilingual usage and stricter latency targets (95th percentile constraints) require us to re-evaluate model variants (architecture & quantization trade-offs) and introduce a formal upgrade process that accounts for locale-specific regressions and tail latency under batching and KV-cache warmstart conditions.

Deliverables: candidate matrix (model sizes, quantization levels, locale coverage), regression harness + baseline metrics, perf profiles (median/95/99 latencies, GPU throughput, cost-per-query), canary rollout plan with A/B metrics and automated rollback gates, runbook for oncall and SEs, and a PRD summarizing recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: A shortlist of 3-5 candidate cross-encoder variants with rationale and expected trade-offs (quality vs latency vs cost)
Offline regression harness implemented that computes NDCG@10 / MRR across English + top-8 locales and produces diffs versus baseline
Synthetic and replay-based latency profiles showing median and 95th latencies at target QPS (target: median < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for mixed-locale traffic) for each candidate
Canary rollout config that runs 1%, 10%, 25% traffic stages with automated gates on quality and latency and a documented rollback procedure
Fallback policy defined: if candidate fails SLOs, service should route to compact fallback model with documented quality degradation bounds
Runbook and Console dashboard artifacts linked in PRD and ready for review by SRE and PM
All code and configs landed in GitHub with tests and a production smoke test that runs on deploy
success_metrics: Net ranking quality: no more than 1% drop in NDCG@10 for any supported locale; preferred improvement >=1.5% overall
Latency: median latency at target load reduced or unchanged; p95 latency does not regress by more than 10% compared to baseline
Cost: cost-per-rerank token change within +/- 10% or justified by quality gains
Scaling: candidate passes throughput target of 200 QPS per GPU for quantized variants (when applicable)
Operational: canary rollback automation triggers correctly in at least 2 simulated failure scenarios
